80100.subject: MetaMask Pulls Its Validators Out of Lido
80100.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[MetaMask Staking](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/metamask-staking-exits-lido-validators-after-infrastructure-compromise)**[ began exiting its Lido validators after an infrastructure compromise, with up to 45 days to re-enter](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/metamask-staking-exits-lido-validators-after-infrastructure-compromise)

* **[Hyperliquid](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/onchain-perps-close-execution-gap-with-centralized-exchanges)**[ matched centralized depth on four of five crypto assets and cost less all-in, Castle Labs found](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/onchain-perps-close-execution-gap-with-centralized-exchanges)

* **[World Liberty](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/world-liberty-launches-wlfi-staking-plans-1-25m-usd1-pool)**[ opened WLFI staking with a $1.25M USD1 pool, a 180-day lock and a voting requirement](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/world-liberty-launches-wlfi-staking-plans-1-25m-usd1-pool)

* **[EIP-8363's authors](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/authors-pull-ethereum-staking-reward-burn-from-hegot)**[ pulled the Ethereum staking reward burn out of the Hegotá upgrade](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/authors-pull-ethereum-staking-reward-burn-from-hegot)

* **[Judge Rochon](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/judge-dismisses-libra-m3m3-class-action-with-prejudice)**[ dismissed the LIBRA and M3M3 class action with prejudice, finding six months too short for RICO](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/judge-dismisses-libra-m3m3-class-action-with-prejudice)

Exiting an Ethereum validator and getting the ETH back are separate events. Lido put the distance between them at up to 45 days: the exit, then the sweep to a withdrawal address, then a queue to get back in.

MetaMask Staking [began exiting the validators it operates inside Lido](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/metamask-staking-exits-lido-validators-after-infrastructure-compromise) after an infrastructure compromise, according to Lido's Sept. 30 disclosure. MetaMask said on Oct. 1 that it found no indication wallets or customer funds were affected, and called the exits precautionary. Lido expects the last of them out by Oct. 7, told stETH holders no action is required, and warned of foregone rewards and downtime penalties if validators go offline. Neither company has said how the infrastructure was compromised. Sentora's Morpho vaults [saw sharp outflows](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sentora-s-morpho-vaults-see-sharp-outflows-amid-metamask-staking-incident) overnight.

It was less than three months ago when Consensys [halted MetaMask releases in July over a North Korea-linked contractor](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/consensys-halted-metamask-releases-over-north-korea-linked-contractor). Today in AI NOW & BEYOND 🔥 Deploy Self-Hosted AI Agents Deploy Self-Hosted AI Agents with One-Click Setup AI Highlights of the Week Too Important to Miss Deploy Self-Hosted AI Agents with One-Click Setup Sponsored AI agents are becoming capable of much more than answering questions. They can handle recurring research, run scheduled tasks, remember context across sessions, and develop new skills over time. OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are built to bring these capabilities to self-hosted environments. With one-click Marketplace apps on Vultr, you can deploy them on cloud infrastructure and start building your own AI-powered workflows. Launch OpenClaw & Hermes Agent Instantly Claude Helped Researchers Break Into OpenAI Three researchers reached employee accounts and internal repositories in less than 72 hours Hacktron researchers combined flaws in OpenAI’s community forum and login system to take over employee accounts. With Claude’s help, they demonstrated access to internal repositories without reading the code, then reported their findings. Key Points: New Model, Different Result: Opus 4.8 struggled to build a working exploit, but Opus 5 succeeded within hours of its release. Codex Proved the Breach: The team used an employee’s Codex account to submit a harmless proposed change to OpenAI’s private code repository. A Surprisingly Small Bill: Their wider investigation across several companies cost under $3,000 in AI tokens, with three researchers doing the work. Fixed and Rewarded: OpenAI confirmed its fix roughly 14 hours after the report and paid $6,500 for the OpenAI vulnerability, not the forum attack. Why It Matters: AI is making sophisticated hacking cheaper, though skilled researchers still guided this work. The warning for businesses is how far one compromised account can reach when AI assistants connect it to code, email and other company tools. Happy Thursday! *Bitcoin* is up today, trading around *$84,700* , while *U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs* ended a nine-day, *$3 billion* inflow streak as *$149 million* exited the funds on Wednesday.

Also in today's newsletter, *NEAR Intents* suffered a *$3.8 million* *exploit* , *Lloyds* and *Visa* settled *$750,000* using *USDC* in a live cross-border pilot, *Hyperliquid Policy Center* and *Circle* are pushing for changes to EU crypto rules, and more.

*THE BIG ONE*

*📉 Bitcoin ETFs snap 9-day, $3.1 billion inflow streak*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-10-01-bitcoin-etfs-9-day-3-billion-inflow-streak-comes-to-an-end-as-149-million-exits-the-funds-417384?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs* recorded *$148.7 million in combined net outflows* on Wednesday, ending a nine-day streak that brought in *$3.1 billion*.

* *BlackRock's IBIT* also ended its own nine-day inflow run, which had brought in $1.6 billion, with *$9.5 million in net outflows* on Wednesday.
* *Fidelity's FBTC* led the day's outflows with *$125.6 million* , followed by *Bitwise's BITB* with $13.6 million. All remaining funds registered zero flows.
